articles.title: Bridging the Gap: Applying Infrastructure Discipline to Probabilistic AI Systems
articles.excerpt: When transitioning from building high-scale platform infrastructure to engineering production AI environments, a fundamental architectural shift becomes clear. Having spent years designing resilient e…
articles.body: When transitioning from building high-scale platform infrastructure to engineering production AI environments, a fundamental architectural shift becomes clear. Having spent years designing resilient environments at hyperscale - managing more than 60,000 servers and supporting over 100 million users - I have built my approach around a core principle: infrastructure must be engineered for predictable behavior under defined conditions. Traditional distributed systems are never perfectly deterministic. Concurrency, hardware degradation, and network failures constantly introduce uncertainty. However, our operational methodologies - SysOps, DevOps, and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) - are designed to mitigate that uncertainty and maintain reliable, predictable system behavior.

articles.body: To check your phone for stalkerware, look in the places spying apps need to hide. On Android, go through your full app list (including system apps), then check Device admin apps, Accessibility, Notification access and Install unknown apps, and run a Google Play Protect scan. On iPhone, open Settings, Privacy & Security, Safety Check (iOS 16 or later), look for unknown profiles under General, VPN & Device Management, and check which devices are signed in to your Apple Account. Most stalkerware needs someone to have had your unlocked phone or your account password. Important: if you think a partner or ex is monitoring you, removing the app can alert them, so contact a domestic abuse helpline from a different, safe device before you change anything.

articles.title: How We Turned 30 Restaurant Nutrition PDFs into Calculators
articles.excerpt: Restaurant chains publish their nutrition facts, but rarely in a form you can use while ordering. Chipotle's guide lists every ingredient on its own row. Domino's lists toppings per serving, separatel…
articles.body: Restaurant chains publish their nutrition facts, but rarely in a form you can use while ordering. Chipotle's guide lists every ingredient on its own row. Domino's lists toppings per serving, separately for each crust and size. Subway lists a 6-inch sub, and you work out the footlong yourself. None of them adds up the order you are actually about to eat. So we built TrayFacts : one calculator per chain, built only from each chain's official numbers. You tap what goes in your bowl, sub, or box, and the calories, protein, carbs, fat, and sodium add up as you go. It now covers 30 chains and more than 10,000 menu items, sizes, and ingredients. This post is about the parts that turned out harder than expected. 1. Getting the data: every chain is different There is no common format.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
